content.text:
It isn’t anything in your dotfiles that’s broken – it’s your Homebrew‐installed Stow still pointing at a non‑existent perl 5.30 interpreter. The first line of `/opt/homebrew/bin/stow` is:

```perl
#!/usr/bin/perl5.30
```
【F: /opt/homebrew/bin/stow†L1】

macOS no longer ships perl5.30 at `/usr/bin/perl5.30`, so you get the “bad interpreter” error.

---  

### Easiest / recommended fix

Reinstall Stow via Homebrew so that it picks up whatever Perl you actually have on your machine:

```shell
brew reinstall stow
```

Once that’s done, rerun your `stow -d --target=$HOME .codex` and it should work.

---

### Alternative (manual) workaround

If you’d rather just hack the shebang in the script yourself, you can edit the first line to use `env`:

```diff
--- /opt/homebrew/bin/stow.orig    2023-XX-XX 12:34:56.000000000 -0700
+++ /opt/homebrew/bin/stow        2023-XX-XX 12:35:10.000000000 -0700
@@ -1,1 +1,1 @@
-#!/usr/bin/perl5.30
+#!/usr/bin/env perl
```

That’ll force it to pick up whichever Perl is first on your `PATH` (e.g. the system Perl at `/usr/bin/perl` or one you’ve installed via `perlbrew`/`plenv`/Homebrew).

---

Let me know if you hit any other snags!
